feature: E1-C residential access in a graph with bound bridges
source_identity: Tested working bytes committed with this report; LF-normalized SHA survives checkout newline conversion.

engine.renderer: Vulkan Forward+ / AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX

scope: UI and current 3D loopback HTTP use the same candidate and transaction; request schema unchanged, bridge summary added.
Mixed native stone_bridge and waterway bridge_ref; target ordinary straight ground road adjoining stone bridge.

Protected/missing/modified bridge, locked/modified waterway member, invalid bridge endpoint/width, direct bridge/bridgehead target, real corridor obstruction and changed bridge-only texture reject atomically.
Bridge, river ownership, terrain and scope-external road values and identities preserved; one undo/redo; native save/reopen.
Four kerb volume cases: clear approach, actual wing collision, bridge body, unknown frozen payload.
Four exterior routes use native saved geometry, 58 production colliders and WorldAuthority movement; every route grounded with no rejected moves.
Native static batching retained: mixed fixture 16 to 2 render surfaces, 12852 vertices unchanged, zero pending groups; this is a correctness check, not a performance claim.
limitations: Ordinary heightfield support and straight ground target only; bridge deck/bridgehead joins and terrain editing remain outside this operation.
Runtime evidence uses the production movement authority and a capsule, without player avatar rendering or full game streaming readiness; no repeated house interior review.
Waterway bridge_ref ownership is covered by HTTP; physical walks cover the stone bridge and residential exterior, not the separate legacy waterway bridge.
Reopen permits only 1e-10 numeric serialization difference; observed maximum 4.44089209850063e-16. Existing bridge/river/outside-scope records additionally checked for exact numeric equality.
No formal map content, new art asset delivery, performance project, push or merge.
Each new candidate continues to report requires_runtime_verification; one fixture does not prove arbitrary future placement.
development_findings: Initial mixed graph exposed a conservative kerb vs whole-bridge-bounds false positive; fixed by reusing frozen approach triangle checks with the complete kerb prism.

An overly strict test of newly generated double precision numbers across native serialization observed 4.44e-16 roundtrip difference. Final regression records the maximum and enforces 1e-10; no geometry tolerance in production was widened.
execution: All graphical tests ran via tools/run_godot_background.py on a private inactive Windows desktop with unique temporary maps/packs and loopback ports. CPU connector regression was headless; its default runtime report was copied here and restored from the archived prior report; tracked prior evidence remains unchanged.
